title: What is Asynchronous JavaScript?
overview: Asynchronous JavaScript allows tasks to run independently without blocking the execution of other code. It helps applications handle time-consuming operations efficiently.

title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous
overview: Synchronous code executes line by line and waits for each task to complete. Asynchronous code allows other tasks to continue while waiting for a time-consuming operation.

example.title: Comparison
example.content:
Synchronous:
Task 1 → Task 2 → Task 3

Asynchronous:
Task 1 → Start Task 2 → Task 3 → Task 2 completes later

title: JavaScript Event Loop
overview: The event loop allows JavaScript to handle asynchronous operations even though JavaScript runs on a single thread. It manages execution between the call stack and callback queues.

example.title: Event Loop Flow
example.content:
Call Stack
      ↓
Web APIs
      ↓
Callback Queue
      ↓
Event Loop

title: setTimeout and setInterval
overview: setTimeout executes a function after a specified delay, while setInterval repeatedly executes a function at a fixed time interval.

title: Callbacks
overview: Callbacks are functions passed as arguments to other functions and executed after a task completes. They were one of the first ways to handle asynchronous operations.

example.title: Callback Example

title: Callback Problems
overview: Using many nested callbacks can make code difficult to read and maintain. This problem is known as callback hell.

title: Asynchronous JavaScript in React Native
overview: React Native applications use asynchronous operations for tasks like API calls, file handling, storage operations, and background processes.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how asynchronous JavaScript works, the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code, event loop, timers, callbacks, and its usage in React Native.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Async code does not block execution.
✔ Event loop manages async tasks.
✔ Timers execute delayed tasks.
✔ Callbacks handle completed operations.
✔ React Native uses async operations frequently.
